question: to the Commission Stéphanie Yon-Courtin (Renew) Subject:

In its opinion of 17 July 2026, the French Competition Authority considered the AI agents sector to be already highly concentrated, with Google, OpenAI and Anthropic accounting for over 80 % of usage, and shielded by barriers to entry (computing power, energy, data) and expansion (user access, limited portability and interoperability). It warns of disintermediation, given that as these agents become the main gateway to digital services, they will displace other gateways, hitting publishers and retailers and reducing the diversity of supply. Although virtual assistants already feature on the list of core platform services in Article 2(2) of the Digital Markets Act (DMA), the DMA review declined to address AI services. 1.

Is the Commission prepared to open, without delay, a market investigation under Article 17 DMA to designate providers of AI agents meeting the Article 3 DMA criteria as being gatekeepers, including where the quantitative thresholds are not met?
Will it open a market investigation under Article 19 DMA with a view to proposing the addition of AI agents and marketplaces distributing AI models to the core platform services list, and when?

How will it guarantee freedom of choice, portability and interoperability between AI agents, applying Article 14 DMA to monitor gatekeepers’ acquisitions in competing agents, and Articles 101 and 102 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union to their partnerships?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (24.9.2026)

The Commission is closely monitoring the platform economy under the Digital Markets Act (DMA)1, including the rapid development of AI services and assistants. It is actively gathering information from market participants on the types of AI services available, how they function, and their role for business and end users in the EU. On the basis of this fact-finding, the Commission will decide on further steps. At the same time, ensuring contestability and fairness for AI service providers is a key DMA enforcement priority. In July 2026, the Commission concluded two proceedings2 providing measures to improve access to Google Search data for third-party search services, including AIenabled services, and requiring interoperability on Android so that alternative AI assistants can be easily invoked and access relevant device functionalities on equal terms with Google’s own services. Information received under Article 14 DMA confirms gatekeepers’ strong interest in AI markets, reflected in most of their acquisitions in 2025. The Commission shares this information with Member States to support national merger review or possible referrals. The Commission will continue applying the DMA as well as competition law in a complementary way, where relevant and opportune.
1 Regulation (EU) 2022/1925 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 September 2022 on contestable

and fair markets in the digital sector and amending Directives (EU) 2019/1937 and (EU) 2020/1828 (Digital Markets Act) https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/1925/oj/eng. 2 https://digital-markets-act.ec.europa.eu/commission-provides-guidance-google-ai-interoperability-android-andsharing-google-search-data-under-2026-07-16_en.
